---
title: 'FOLD Token'
description:
  'Frequently asked questions about the FOLD token: its purpose, its utility, and its role in the
  Interfold network.'
---

import { LinkCard, LinkCards } from '@/components/ui'

# FOLD Token

This FAQ runs through what FOLD does in the Interfold network. It's for token holders and for anyone
keen to operate a ciphernode. The questions come in three groups: the role of FOLD,
transferability, and ciphernode operation. For supply and allocation data, have a look at
[FOLD Tokenomics](/tokenomics).

## The role of FOLD

### What role does FOLD play in the Interfold network?

The Interfold is a distributed network for confidential coordination. Applications ask for Encrypted
Execution Environments (E3s), and ciphernodes coordinate and secure each computation.

FOLD is what keeps the economic side of the network ticking over.

### What is the utility of the FOLD token?

FOLD does three main jobs, and all three hang together: ciphernode bonding, protocol
incentives, and governance.

**Ciphernode bonding.** Ciphernode operators bond FOLD so they're eligible for network duties. Bonded
FOLD sits in the `BondingRegistry` contract. When the bond owner (the wallet that funds the bond)
unbonds it, the FOLD waits in an exit queue before the bond owner can claim it back. Bonded FOLD may be
subject to protocol-defined withdrawal periods. It may also cop penalties for provable
misbehaviour or for not doing the responsibilities it's been assigned. That way, whoever's running
the node has their own money riding on doing the job properly.

**Protocol incentives.** Ciphernode operators get a share of the fees from completed E3s. On top of
that, they may pick up FOLD incentives for successfully finishing protocol-defined duties as
members of an E3 committee.

**Governance.** FOLD is expected to give holders a say in governance through the Interfold DAO.
That may cover decisions about network parameters, protocol upgrades, and how the treasury's run.
Governance processes may include secret-ballot mechanisms that run on the Interfold network
itself. For the current voting rules, see [Governance](/governance).

## Transferability

### When did FOLD become generally transferable?

General FOLD transferability could be switched on at or after Aug 19 at **14:00 UTC (10 AM ET)**.

From Unix timestamp **`1787148000`** on, anyone could call the `tge()` function on the FOLD
contract to enable general transferability. Once that transaction went through, FOLD became generally
transferable.

That transaction ran on Aug 19, 2026 at 14:00:23 UTC. `tgeTimestamp()` on the FOLD contract returns
`1787148023`, so FOLD is generally transferable now, no worries.

Mind you, general FOLD transferability and Network Alpha are two separate milestones in the wider
Interfold launch sequence. For more on that, see [FOLD Transferability](/faq/transferability).

## Ciphernode operation

### How can I use FOLD to operate a ciphernode?

Operating a ciphernode is designed to be permissionless: nobody has to sign off on it. The setup
comes in four parts:

1. Provision cloud-based or personal hardware.
2. Run the ciphernode software.
3. Bond FOLD to the ciphernode.
4. Complete on-chain registration.

Once the ciphernode's registered, it can take part in E3 committees whenever the protocol rules
pick it. To be in the running for committee selection, a registered ciphernode also needs a minimum ticket
balance. See [Tickets and sortition](/operate/tickets-and-sortition).

For the current setup requirements, bonding instructions, and operator documentation, head over to
[Ciphernode Operators](/operate) and [Registration and bonding](/operate/registration).

### Can I delegate my FOLD to a ciphernode operator?

Nah. The Interfold's bonding model is operator-only, and that's on purpose. Every FOLD that's bonded to a
ciphernode is capital at risk for the operator that runs it.

Delegated capital would let operators run ciphernodes they only partly own. That'd water down
accountability and weaken the network's economic security guarantees.

In the `BondingRegistry` contract, each ciphernode has one bond owner, and only the bond owner can
bond FOLD to it. The operator picks the bond owner, which can be the operator address or a
separate wallet, say a cold wallet or a Safe.

## Support

If you need a hand, jump into the official [Telegram group](https://t.me/enclave_e3).
